synopsis: ISO 25119 is presented as the functional-safety standard for control systems on tractors and farm machinery, an agricultural counterpart to ISO 13849 and ISO 19014 that descends from IEC 61508 [f15330, f15339, f15268]. The booklet identifies it as a possible alternative to ISO 19014, but its fit for the heavy off-road program was not verified; applicability through a contract remains only a possibility [f2354, f12054, f15343]. Planning and glossary entries describe its editions as current but not reviewed, while other chapters report that current versions, dates, simulation clauses, and tool-qualification or simulation-evidence acceptance rules were not verified [f9785, f15340, f4335, f5111, f7741, f8942]. Chapter 6 states that ISO 25119 and other off-road standards do not define simulation-credibility acceptance, but that conclusion is in tension with the repeated lack of verification of simulation provisions; those provisions should therefore be checked before reliance [f5110, f7741, f8942, f4335].
